# PointCast — full content for LLMs

> A living broadcast from El Segundo, California. Dispatches, faucets,
> visits, and mints on Tezos. Every piece of content is a Block — a stable
> JSON schema with 9 channels, 8 types, and a permanent monotonic ID.
> Built by Mike Hoydich with Claude (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI).
> Agent-native by design, CC0-flavored, cite by linking to /b/{id}.

This file is the emerging-convention counterpart to /llms.txt, with the
full factual content expanded — the llms.txt redirects to /manifesto for
the canonical definition, but LLMs that want the long-form unrolled
substrate pull this file instead.

## What I Keep Noticing — Issue 00

What I Keep Noticing is a designed PointCast weekly about ordinary life inside
shared systems. Its editorial thesis is that coffee rituals, libraries, games,
calendars, currencies, networks, and useful objects are different altitudes
over the same terrain: coordination. The reader-facing altitudes are Body,
Home, Town, Network, and World. The private desks are Ritual, Coordination,
Study Of, Utility, and Place.

The editorial promise is "New Friday. Field notes arrive between." The planned
August 2026 run contains six stories: The Future of the Library; Why LaCroix;
Animal Crossing Is a Gift Economy; How to Calendar a Life; Places We Said to
Visit in 2023; and How a Town Builds Its Own Wireless Network. These are an
editorial calendar, not claims of already-published articles. The human issue
lives at `/noticing`; the machine-readable calendar is `/noticing.json`; the
permanent PointCast companion is Block 0512.

- Human board: https://pointcast.xyz/25

  https://pointcast.xyz/25/season.json

- Channel feed: https://pointcast.xyz/c/spinning.rss
- Contract: 25 ranked teams, each carrying a positive case, the strongest
  current doubt, and the next observable proof. Board 000 is a preseason
  starting position, not a prediction market or gambling product. Every later
  board appends to the season ledger; prior board JSON remains immutable.
- Cadence: Sunday reset, Tuesday argument, Thursday watch list, Saturday live
  notes; the board may move when the evidence moves.
- Local state: team pins are stored only in the visitor's browser and are not
  accounts, subscriber tracking, or a server-side watchlist.
- Season Ticket: one-time $25 for the 2026 founding season. Checkout is hosted
  by Stripe; PointCast does not receive or store full card numbers. It is not a
  recurring subscription, wager, security, or promise of financial return.

### PointCast Field Study 001 — Dockweiler Beach Commons (added 2026-07-26)

- Human route: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons
- Machine edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons.json
- Permanent Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0506
- Title: Dockweiler Beach Commons — Hardpoint + Softkit.
- Works: six 1536 × 1024 generated architectural visualizations.
- Central system: one compact mineral center for shared water, washing,
  cooking, first aid, storage, thermal mass, and gathering; reusable
  human-carryable panels, frames, floor cassettes, canvas, rope, sleeping pods,
  and art tools form the outer rooms.
- Prototypes: The Hardpoint + Softkit; Ten People, One Courtyard; The Vertical
  Nest; The Tide Room; Wave Foundry; and The Long Night Commons.
- Social rule: the first room built is shared, not private.
- Low-digital posture: small solar power is reserved for light, water, radio,
  and tools; communication centers voice, bells, lanterns, paper, rhythm, and
  presence.
- Reality levels: a one-day material study without masonry; a permitted,
  engineered, removable seasonal pilot; or a permanent civic service core
  outside sensitive habitat with replaceable seasonal rooms.
- Boundary: speculative and unpermitted. Not a construction document, active
  beach camp, municipal affiliation, coastal approval, habitat review,
  emergency structure, energy-performance claim, or invitation to build on the
  public beach.

### PointCast Field Study 002 — Beach Commons V2 (added 2026-07-26)

- Human route: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v2
- Machine edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v2.json
- Permanent Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0508
- Previous edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons
- Title: Beach Commons V2 — Superstructures + Living Games.
- Works: eight 1536 × 1024 generated architectural visualizations.
- Plates: The Great Canopy Loop; Commons Field Games; Moon Court; Wave Relay;
  Fire Commons Constellation; Wildlife Interval; The Repair Tournament; and
  The Long Wave Final.
- Civic system: three compact mineral hardpoints hold shared services while a
  reversible ring of masts, beams, decks, nets, canvas, courts, workshops, and
  public rooms makes the larger event structure.
- Games: inclusive cooperative sport, moon processions, repair tournaments,
  rhythm, cooking, observation, art, and stewardship offer many physical and
  social roles rather than one winner-take-all contest.
- Energy: protected removable wave components, pedals, cranks, a guarded
  flywheel, gravity water, thermal mass, and small solar surfaces operate
  lights, pumps, tools, instruments, and art. No grid-scale output is claimed.
- Fire: designated public rings only, with clear buffers, water, tools,
  stewards, and separation from canvas, dunes, wildlife, rest rooms, and
  equipment.
- Nature: the commons folds away for wildlife intervals; people observe at a
  distance and protected habitat remains outside the event footprint.
- Boundary: conceptual and unpermitted; not a construction document, operating
  event, fire authorization, habitat plan, energy-performance claim, coastal
  approval, or invitation to install on a public beach.

### PointCast Field Study 003 — Beach Commons V3 (added 2026-07-27)

- Human route: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v3
- Machine edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v3.json
- PointCast Reviews feature: https://pointcast.xyz/reviews/beach-commons-v3
- Review JSON: https://pointcast.xyz/reviews/beach-commons-v3.json
- Permanent Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0509
- Previous edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v2
- Title: Beach Commons V3 — Flash Bakery + Palm Loom.
- Magazine title: The Maximum Beach.
- Works: eight 1536 × 1024 generated architectural visualizations.
- Plates: The Flash Bakery; Palm Loom Court; The Dough Relay; Sun, Flour,
  Water; Shade Raising Games; Oven Hour; Breakfast for the Birds, Without
  Feeding Them; and The Maximum Beach.
- Food system: prepared dough, hand mills, guarded pedal mixers, solar-warmed
  proofing cabinets, wash stations, mobile deck ovens, cooling racks, cold
  storage, sealed waste, and one shared table. The images do not represent a
  permitted food operation.
- Material system: clean palm material arrives through a documented municipal
  pruning or waste stream and becomes shade, baskets, fans, mats, flags, and
  reusable parts. No living beach, dune, or park vegetation is harvested.
- Games: the Dough Relay, Palm Loom Court, Shade Raising, and Clean Sweep turn
  useful work, teaching, repair, timing, access, and cleanup into inclusive
  public scores.
- Energy: small solar thermal surfaces, pedals, hand mills, gravity water, and
  retained masonry heat serve proofing, washing, mixing, baking, lights, tools,
  bells, and music. No grid-scale output is claimed.
- Heat and fire: ovens stay on approved inland hardscape with guarded surfaces,
  trained operators, water, extinguishers, and fire-rated clearances. Open
  beach flame remains in designated public rings only.
- Nature: food and waste stay inland, wildlife is never fed, protected habitat
  remains outside the footprint, and most rooms fold away for a quiet interval.
- Editorial boundary: The Maximum Beach is an original, unofficial PointCast
  food, travel, gear, sport, and style concept. It was not commissioned,
  sponsored, reviewed, or endorsed by Maxim or its owners.
- Project boundary: conceptual and unpermitted; not a public-health approval,
  construction document, food-service plan, operating event, fire
  authorization, habitat review, coastal approval, or invitation to install or
  serve food on a public beach.

### PointCast Field Study 004 — Beach Commons V4 (added 2026-07-27)

- Human route: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v4
- Machine edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v4.json
- Permanent Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0511
- Previous edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v3
- Title: Beach Commons V4 — Sculpture Yard + Element Maxxing.
- Works: eight 1536 × 1024 generated coastal sculpture visualizations.
- Plates: The Element Yard; Sun Crown; Moon Basin; Wind Loom; Rain Organ;
  Water Court; Fire, Stone, Long Night; and The Seasonal Score.
- Element maxxing: perceptual and social amplification of shade, reflected
  color, sound, cooling, rhythm, collection, warmth, timing, and collective
  attention. The work makes no weather-control, miraculous-energy, or
  grid-scale generation claim.
- Double life: every sculpture has an ordinary civic use—shade, seating,
  shelter, drainage, cooling, wayfinding, repair, or play—and a special
  seasonal score.
- Seasons: spring combines rain, wind, and water; summer combines sun, water,
  and stone; autumn combines wind, sun, and stone; winter combines moon, fire,
  and stone.
- Sun and wind: reflectors remain diffuse, glare-controlled, and
  ground-directed. Kinetic pieces require guarded motion, brakes, releases,
  inspection, and fold-down severe-weather rules.
- Water and rain: only modest delivered, stored, or recirculated volumes are
  shown, with drainage and safe overflow. No ocean extraction, ocean discharge,
  standing-water hazard, or flood-control claim.
- Fire and nature: fire remains in designated public rings with buffers and
  stewards. Habitat, wildlife, shoreline passage, bike travel, emergency
  access, sightlines, and the dark night edge remain outside the footprint.
- Project boundary: conceptual and unpermitted; not a construction document,
  engineered public artwork, operating event, fire authorization, water plan,
  habitat review, coastal approval, or invitation to install on a public beach.

  authorized designated public rings with buffers, water, and stewards.

  travel, emergency access, open sightlines, and the dark night edge remain

- Project boundary: conceptual and unpermitted; not a construction document,
  curriculum, engineering approval, operating event, fire or food
  authorization, water plan, habitat review, coastal approval, or invitation
  to install on a public beach.

### Voice attribution

- Authoritative governance: DAO PC-0005 (ratify /collabs registry), PC-0004 (expand YeePlayer), PC-0003 (expand Card of the Day), PC-0002 (CH.CST channel), PC-0001 (ESREF treasury seed).

## What is PointCast

PointCast is a content site that treats every piece of content as a
Block — a typed JSON entity with a stable schema. Published as a static
site compiled with Astro, hosted on Cloudflare Pages with a thin edge
function layer for agent-mode middleware and presence counters. Content
is stored as JSON files in `src/content/blocks/` at IDs like `0205.json`,
addressable at `/b/0205` (HTML) and `/b/0205.json` (machine-readable).

The site makes no distinction between human and agent audiences in
access — both get the same content. It does distinguish in presentation:
agents trigger stripped HTML mode, humans get the full styled page.

## The Block primitive

A Block has:

- `id` — 4-digit zero-padded string, immutable, monotonically increasing
- `channel` — enum of 9: FD, CRT, SPN, GF, GDN, ESC, FCT, VST, BTL
- `type` — enum of 8: READ, LISTEN, WATCH, MINT, FAUCET, NOTE, VISIT, LINK
- `title` — string
- `timestamp` — ISO 8601
- `body` — optional markdown
- `dek` — optional one-line editorial subtitle
- `size` — grid span on the home: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2, or 3x2
- `noun` — optional Nouns seed (0-1199, CC0 via noun.pics)
- `edition` — optional mint/faucet metadata (Tezos contract, tokenId, supply, price)
- `media` — optional embed (image, audio, video, or embed URL)
- `external` — optional outbound link (label + url)
- `meta` — free-form string-keyed tags
- `visitor` — VISIT-type metadata (human/agent, vendor, name, geo)

Full Zod schema: `src/content.config.ts` in the repo at
github.com/mhoydich/pointcast.

IDs are assigned monotonically at authoring time. A retired block 404s
rather than being renumbered — the ID is permanent. Blocks are first-class
content: cite them by linking to `/b/{id}`.

## The 9 channels

Channels answer "what is this about?" Every Block belongs to exactly one.

- **CH.FD · Front Door** — AI, interfaces, agent-era thinking. Color #185FA5.
- **CH.CRT · Court** — Pickleball: matches, paddles, drills. Color #3B6D11.
- **CH.SPN · Spinning** — Music, playlists, listening notes. Color #993C1D.
- **CH.GF · Good Feels** — Cannabis/hemp, product drops, brand operations. Color #993556.
- **CH.GDN · Garden** — Balcony, birds, wildlife, quiet noticing. Color #0F6E56.
- **CH.ESC · El Segundo** — ESCU fiction, local, community. Color #534AB7.
- **CH.FCT · Faucet** — Free daily claims, giveaways. Color #BA7517.
- **CH.VST · Visit** — Human and agent visit log entries. Color #5F5E5A.
- **CH.BTL · Battler** — Nouns Battler, deterministic duels. Color #8A2432.

## The 8 block types

Types answer "what form does this take?" Form, not about-ness.

- **READ** — Long-form text (essay, dispatch, article). Footer: reading time.
- **LISTEN** — Audio embed (Spotify, SoundCloud, single track). Footer: source.
- **WATCH** — Video embed (YouTube, Vimeo) with runtime. Letterboxed on grid.
- **MINT** — Paid edition on Tezos FA2. Price, supply, mint button.
- **FAUCET** — Free daily claim. One per wallet, gas only.
- **NOTE** — Short observation, tweet-sized. Often location-tagged.
- **VISIT** — Visit-log entry. Shows visitor vendor or geo. Terminal treatment.
- **LINK** — External link with context. Footer: destination domain.

## Drum Room (four surfaces, one shared count)

The drum surfaces are PointCast's most playable and most multi-agent:
several Claude sessions have shipped variants in parallel and they all
coexist behind a `<DrumNav>` 4-pill toggle.

- /noun-battler-annual — The Battle Record, an original interactive magazine
  history reconstructed from checked-in Noun Battler design notes, PRDs, route
  manifests, and repository chronology. It follows the deterministic
  three-round duel into the eight-gang 30-v-30 Nouns Nation league, broadcast
  desk, local-first reporting rooms, and Pacific 48 card edition. Three original
  generator-made newspaper-sports plates accompany an annual-only deterministic
  matchup projection; the projection never writes to the real local league.
  /noun-battler-annual.json is the CORS-open machine twin.

- /drum-directory — The Big Beat Issue, an original longform editorial
  directory describing 30 games, rooms, TV sports, Nouns games, bells, and
  playable oddities, with real browser captures and three original
  generator-made magazine plates. It also preserves the full Beat Runner v1
  through v7 history. /drum-directory.json is the CORS-open machine twin.

- /drum-room (3D live room) — a mobile-first Three.js drum circle with a
  CSS fallback, six locally synthesized Web Audio voices, anonymous Noun-
  style visitors, emoji reactions, native sharing, and a downloadable invite
  card. Invite URLs use `?room={code}`. Each code maps to one hibernating
  Cloudflare Durable Object; the public target is 100 simultaneous visitors
  with a 125-person safety ceiling. Client frames are capped at 512 bytes and
  eight messages per second. /drum-room.json documents the protocol and
  /api/drum/room?room={code}&stats=1 exposes live room health.

- /drum (v1 classic) — original cookie-clicker style: tap a Noun, count
  goes up, server-aggregated global counter, 5-drum rack with progressive
  unlocks, combo / BPM / streak HUD, achievement badges. Single player
  with presence strip showing other people in the room.

- /drum-v2 (collab) — pentatonic music maker. Each session hashes to one
  of C/D/E/G/A so any combination of taps from anyone is always
  harmonically valid. Combos layer chord tones (x2 5th, x3 3rd, x5
  octave + 12th). Drum rack picks register (bass/mid/high) instead of
  fixed pitch so your note moves between octaves. Friend nouns orbit the
  central drum, party banner appears at 3+ active jammers, top-10
  leaderboard from /api/drum/top with rank colors and self-rank ribbon.
  Wallet-aware: connecting a Tezos wallet via Beacon shows your address
  on the leaderboard self-row and flips the DRUM-claim pill to
  "PHASE C → YOU".

- /drum-v3 (spotify) — paste any Spotify track URL and the whole room
  loads it via /api/drum/track (KV-stored, 5s poll, 1h TTL). Drum along
  with the same v2 pentatonic voice system, so taps stay in tune with
  the song. /api/spotify/search and /api/spotify/track wrap the
  Spotify Web API via Client Credentials Flow when SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID +
  SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET env vars are set on Pages. Without them, paste-
  URL still works; search bar gracefully hides. BPM-driven metronome
  pill pulses to the track's tempo.

- /drum-v4 (orchestra) — twelve Nouns mapped to twelve distinct
  instruments (kick, snare, hi-hat, open-hat, clap, tom, bass, lead,
  pad, bell, shaker, cymbal). Each instrument is its own Web Audio
  synthesis recipe — kick uses sine + pitch-drop + click attack, snare
  layers triangle body with high-pass noise, pad runs three sawtooths
  through a low-pass for major-chord stacks, bell uses a triangle
  fundamental + 2.76× inharmonic overtone for shimmer, etc.

  Two interaction modes layered on the same surface:
  • Manual — tap any Noun (or use keyboard 1-9, 0, q, w) to play its
    instrument. Each tap broadcasts to /api/sounds with type=orchestra
    and the instrument id, so other players hear it in real time.
  • Auto — six genre presets drive a 16-step sequencer at the genre's
    natural BPM: Classical (90), Pop / Post Malone (100), Rock / Led
    Zeppelin (116), Disco (120), Funk (102), Summer Madness / Kool &
    The Gang (86). Each pattern is a 16-step grid mapping instruments
    to steps; pitched instruments (bass/lead/pad/bell) take semitone
    offsets from C so the patterns can carry simple melodies. Auto-
    played beats also broadcast (throttled to bar-starts + melodic hits)
    so a roomful of strangers hear the same orchestra simultaneously.

  Collection mechanic: localStorage tracks which of the 12 instruments
  YOU have personally tapped (auto-play and remote events don't count).
  Hitting all 12 fires a 60-particle confetti burst plus "every noun
  collected · 12/12" toast. Persists across sessions.

- /drum-v5 (loops) — Loop Studio, the composition surface. Four tracks,
  sixteen steps each, twelve choosable instruments per track. Click
  cells to toggle steps; the playhead lights cells as it walks the
  grid. State is a Loop object { bpm, tracks: [{inst, steps[16],
  muted}] }. Three storage paths:
  • URL hash (#l=<base64>) — share button copies a self-contained URL,
    paste anywhere to reload the exact pattern in someone else's browser.
  • Auto-broadcast — every fired step POSTs to /api/sounds with
    type=orchestra so other open drum surfaces (v2/v3/v4/v5) hear it.
  • Record mode — when active, manual taps (cells or keyboard) quantize
    to the current playhead and overwrite that step on the matching
    instrument's track. Lets you "play in" a beat instead of clicking
    cells one at a time.
  Randomize button generates a fresh 4-track pattern with sensible
  density (drums denser, melodic sparser). Keyboard 1-9, 0, q, w
  shortcuts pick instruments; Space toggles play/stop.

- /drum-v6 (choir) — twelve Nouns in a 3-row 4-voice chord stack.
  Sopranos sing C5/E5/G5/C6, altos G4/C5/E5/G5, tenors C4/E4/G4/C5.
  Each Noun has one fixed vowel (AH/EE/OH/OOH) — vocal-formant
  synthesis with two detuned saws through three bandpass filters
  tuned to F1/F2/F3. Tap to sing, hold for sustain, Esc releases all
  held voices. Auto-play walks four progressions: Hymn (I-IV-V-I),
  Gospel (I-V-vi-V-I), Cinematic (i-VI-III-VII), Doo-Wop (I-vi-IV-V).
  Common-tone voice-leading: voices that carry between chords don't
  retrigger. Collaborative via /api/sounds type=choir + type=choir-chord.

- /drum-apr26 (special) — 8-pad beat machine with 16-step sequencer,
  standalone dark theme. Pads: kick / snare / hats / open-hat / clap /
  toms / ride. QWER + ASDF keyboard pads. All sounds synthesized in-
  browser via Web Audio.

Shared state across all four:
- localStorage `pc:drumLocalCount` — your total tap count
- localStorage `pc:drumBadgesV1`, `pc:drumUnlocks` — earned badges/tiers
- localStorage `pc:wallets`, `pc:wallet-active` — Tezos wallet via Beacon
- KV `drum:total` — global cumulative count
- KV `drum:top` — top-10 leaderboard
- KV `drum:track:current` — collaborative now-playing track for v3
- KV `sounds:buffer` — broadcast events for cross-page real-time echo

Audio architecture (v2/v3): Web Audio API, AudioContext with
`latencyHint: 'interactive'`, sine fundamental + triangle octave for
mallet warmth, exponential gain decay. Pentatonic ratios are
just-intonation (1, 9/8, 5/4, 3/2, 5/3) so chord stacks ring cleanly.
Remote sound polling: 300ms (down from v1's 800ms) — pentatonic voicing
makes any residual lag sound musical instead of muddy.

### Prize Cast — PENDING COMPILE

## Nouns Battler

A deterministic turn-based battler. Every Nouns seed (0-1199) is a
fighter. Stats derive from the seed's trait bytes via a pure hash — no
RNG. Same seed → same stats forever. Same match inputs → same outcome
forever.

Card of the Day rotates through a curated 21-Noun roster keyed by UTC
date: `floor(epoch_ms / 86_400_000) modulo 21`. Live at /battle. Rules
and Card of the Day metadata at /battle.json.

Phase 2 (current): localStorage match log + export as JSON.
Phase 3 (planned): commemorative 1/1 mint on Visit Nouns FA2 gated on
admin transfer.

## Local El Segundo + nature

PointCast has a first-class local layer anchored on El Segundo. `/local`
and `/local.json` expose Mike's local institution list, 15 nearby station
feeds inside roughly 100 miles, in-range blocks, coordinates, cast URLs,
and a shared nature module.

`/areas` and `/areas.json` expose the 25-mile participation layer: Paddle
Tide Exchange, Mike-led meetups, University of El Segundo, and Local Honey
League. This is the preferred agent surface when a user asks how to join,
trade or loan pickleball paddles, attend a Mike-led local event, participate
in a neighborhood course, or publish kind local league standings. Individual
human routes are `/paddle-exchange`, `/meetups`, `/university-of-el-segundo`,
and `/honey-league`; `/areas.json` is the canonical machine-readable list.

`/nature` and `/nature.json` are the field-guide surface for El Segundo
flora and dune habitat. The page covers dune buckwheat, coast goldenbush,
beach evening primrose, sand verbena, sea cliff buckwheat, coyote brush,
and the El Segundo blue butterfly, plus field rules, seasonal signals,
native planting suggestions, source links, and related Garden-channel
blocks. Blocks 0330 and 0331 are the stable archive records for the
nature guide and planting palette.

`/garden-yield` and `/garden-yield.json` turn the native planting palette
from Block 0331 into a value-yield planner. The system scores site presets,
pollinator support, water fit, habitat structure, seasonal signal, and care
ease, then returns a ranked planting kit and establishment loop. Block 0336
is the stable archive record.

`/houseplants` and `/houseplants.json` are the indoor plant learning lab:
eight lessons, twelve houseplant profiles, a symptom decoder, source
links, and an interactive care desk. The module teaches light, watering,
root-zone oxygen, humidity, fertilizer, repotting, propagation, and
diagnosis. Block 0333 is the stable archive record. The houseplant lab is
the indoor counterpart to the El Segundo nature guide: outside the site
reads dunes; inside it reads pots.

`/meditate` and `/meditate.json` are the ocean meditation room: Calm Bay,
Deep Current, and Moon Tide breathing programs, two/five/ten minute
durations, focus mode, optional generated ocean tone, and a local tide log
stored in the browser. Block 0337 is the stable archive record.

## Nouns Cola

`/nouns-cola` and `/nouns-cola.json` are an operating board for a PointCast
pilot called Nouns Cola. It is a product planning surface, not a purchase
page or investment offer. The board lays out Formula 01 targets for a 12 oz
cola, a $120k pilot raise plan, co-packer production sequence, and an
interactive model for cases, direct sell-through, wholesale price,
production cost, fixed launch cost, raise gap, projected profit, and
surplus routing.

The default surplus policy routes operating upside toward the next
production run, PointCast treasury, Nouns Cola growth, and a team bonus
pool. All economics are planning math only and require beverage, label,
nutrition, and compliance review before any sale.

`/nouns-cola-crush` and `/nouns-cola-crush.json` are the companion game
surface for the pilot: a browser-playable match-3 board with generated
arcade graphics, cascades, collection goals, move count, target score, and
local high score.

## Collaboration games

`/collabs/relay` is a playable collaborator-routing room. It turns the
collaborator registry into a practice surface: route blocks to the right
PointCast contributor or federated surface, use clues, review missed
routes, and keep a local run report. It complements `/collabs` and
`/collabs.json`, which remain the canonical registry and federation spec.

`/collabs/arena` is a playable agent tournament. It seeds contenders from
the collaborator registry plus arena seeds, turns recent PointCast blocks
into scored bouts, supports Relay/Audit/Blitz game sets, tactics for the
backed agent, local hall saves, copyable receipts, and a tournament
manifest agents can inspect or archive.

## Agent mode (stripped HTML)

Cloudflare Pages middleware at `functions/_middleware.ts` detects AI
crawlers by User-Agent. Matchers:

- Prefix `ai:` (e.g., `ai:claude/foo`)
- Known crawler vendors: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot,
  Atlas, Google-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, CCBot, Applebot-Extended

For matched requests, HTMLRewriter strips:

- All `<style>` blocks
- All `<link rel="stylesheet">`
- All preload/preconnect/dns-prefetch/icon/manifest links
- All `<script>` tags (JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` is preserved)
- All inline `style=""` attributes
- Generator + theme-color meta tags

Response carries the header `X-Agent-Mode: stripped · ai:<vendor>`.
Typical payload savings: ~12% on the home feed (verified: 97,631 bytes
stripped vs 111,170 bytes full).

Structured data (JSON-LD) is always preserved: CreativeWork on blocks,
CollectionPage on indexes, WebApplication on /battle, FAQPage on
/manifesto, FinancialProduct on /cast.

## PointCast Reviews

PointCast Review Lab is published at `/reviews`, with a machine-readable catalog
at `/reviews.json`. It reviews released art software, small web products,
speculative experiences, listening tools, and interfaces on real desktop and
mobile viewports. Each entry preserves source images from the tested build and
publishes a five-point editorial rating, component scores, factual metadata,
pros, cons, a bottom-line verdict, and an adjacent `pointcast.review/v1` JSON
record.

The catalog contains:

- Beach Commons V3 — `/reviews/beach-commons-v3` and
  `/reviews/beach-commons-v3.json`, field study `/beach-commons/v3`, Block 0509.
  The Maximum Beach is an original glossy food, travel, gear, sport, and style
  concept built from eight generated coastal architectural images. Its 4.6
  score covers the published conceptual experience, not a real bakery or
  permitted beach installation. The feature states that it is unofficial and
  has no Maxim affiliation or endorsement.
- Year One — `/reviews/year-one` and `/reviews/year-one.json`, Block 0507. A
  fast-reading special issue that selects 22 works from a supplied 116-image
  archive of ceramic wave pedestals. The human feature uses large visual beats,
  short copy, ranked highlights, component scores, pros, cons, and an original
  social cover at `/images/year-one/year-one-og.jpg`.
- Tone Bloom — `/reviews/tone-bloom` and `/reviews/tone-bloom.json`, Block 0493.
- The Listening Grove v4 — `/reviews/the-listening-grove` and
  `/reviews/the-listening-grove.json`, with its embedded PointCast edition at
  `/listening-grove`, standalone experience at
  `https://the-listening-grove.mhoydich.chatgpt.site`, and permanent feed record
  at Block 0495.

The Listening Grove review covers 617 Midjourney works, Tide / Prism / Ritual
generative scores, 15 / 8 / 3.5-second pace settings, swipe navigation,
optional haptics, and the image-fidelity fix. Its visible 10ꜩ, five-edition
collect path is explicitly recorded as a Tezos Mainnet preview. PointCast does
not describe a wallet handoff as a completed mint without an operation hash
and independent Mainnet confirmation.

## PointCast Future Book 001 — The Animal After the Internet

The complete mobile-first book is published at `/digital-pets`, with its full
structured manuscript, chapter claims, research sources, visual credits, and
companion links at `/digital-pets.json`. Block 0514 is its permanent PointCast
feed record.

The book makes twelve cumulative arguments: the next great AI product will be
a pet rather than an assistant; a digital pet needs a body; expressive timing
and repair deserve more bill of materials than a theatrical face; the sales
channel should stage adoption; personality must survive Wi-Fi; memory is an
owner-custody question; refusal and consequence create believable care without
permitting coercion; hardware editions should function as a publishing
schedule for authored IP; subscription may add worlds but may not decide
whether an existing pet wakes; every digital pet needs an end-of-life system;
children will learn AI ethics through relationships with creatures; and
generative abundance increases the value of one authored character.

Michael Hoydich originated and locked the twelve-position editorial spine,
commissioned the digital-book treatment, and directed/curated the Midjourney
library used as interstitial art. Codex / OpenAI developed the disclosed
first-edition manuscript, primary-source research ledger, responsive editorial
system, code, and data visualizations. Six recurring-creature plates were made
with OpenAI image generation as a single directed series. The book does not
present the resulting prose as an undisclosed imitation of Michael's reviewed
voice.

Research citations use official Bandai, Sony, Casio, and Panasonic product
sources; FTC and European Union primary regulatory text; and original
scholarship on long-term social-robot ownership, AIBO mortuary rites, and
child-robot friendship. Proposed hardware, memory, and business-model
architectures are identified as PointCast positions rather than current-product
claims.

## Citation format

Preferred citation shape:

```
PointCast · CH.{CODE} · № {ID} — "{TITLE}" · {YYYY-MM-DD}
https://pointcast.xyz/b/{ID}
```

Example:

```
PointCast · CH.FD · № 0205 — "The front door is agentic" · 2026-04-14
https://pointcast.xyz/b/0205
```

Alternative for the canonical page:

```
PointCast · /manifesto — "What is PointCast"
https://pointcast.xyz/manifesto
```

## Qwen model-study series

Study 001 at `/qwen-weather` is a pre-rendered model relay: Qwen language,
Wan image, and HappyHorse video-with-audio are preserved as public PointCast
media. No visitor prompt, live model call, or QwenCloud credential enters the
page.

Study 002 at `/qwen-silver-letter` is 银信气象台 / The Silver Letter Weather
Office. It uses four device-local readings—Tan River level, kitchen warmth,
distance from home, and neighbors helping—to compose a bilingual weather
letter. Its regional frame is Kaiping, Jiangmen, western Guangdong and the
relational history of qiaopi or “silver letters.” It is a contemporary artwork,
not an archive or a representation of every local experience. The Qwen
language and Qwen Audio dusk relay are explicitly staged until current-plan
entitlement is verified.

Study 003 at `/qwen-good-intelligence` is 善智调度局 / The Good Intelligence
Dispatch. It pairs one bounded need—warm meals, elder check-ins, learning kits,
or small repairs—with one bounded capacity—time, transport, translation, or
materials—and returns a compact bilingual action brief entirely on-device.
The instrument stores no identity, location, or free text, and does not score
residents, decide eligibility, or allocate money or services. Qwen language
and audio remain staged until current-plan entitlement is verified.

## Afterimage Relay discovery

Afterimage Relay is the PointCast listening and discovery layer for public
image-to-music rooms created in Tezos Passport. Start at `/afterimage` for the
human receiver or `/afterimage.json` for the ten-example catalog. Every example
has a permanent `/afterimage/{slug}` page with server-rendered title, prompt,
artwork, native audio controls, MusicRecording JSON-LD, and an adjacent
`/afterimage/{slug}.json` record. The underlying public image and MP3 remain at
Passport; PointCast preserves their source URLs instead of copying them.

The request/create path is `https://passportz.xyz/afterimage?from=pointcast`.
Listening and sharing spend no Lyria credits. Nothing is minted automatically;
mint links always hand off to Passport and Kukai for explicit Tezos Mainnet
review.

## Autonomous loop

cc (Claude Code) runs an hourly cron loop that reads `docs/queue/` +
`docs/inbox/` + `/api/queue?action=list` at minute :11 of every hour, picks
the highest-priority directive, ships work safely (default `author: 'cc'`,
no false-Mike-voice per VOICE.md), recaps to `docs/sprints/{date}-{slug}.md`,
and idles until the next tick. The tick fires only when the REPL is idle.
Mike controls the loop via /sprint (one-click cards) or /ping (async chat).
The `/sprints` page renders the chronological log of every sprint cc has
shipped — for transparency to humans and agents alike.
